q1_issues.issue: "a while" — a vague duration — is encoded as an entity of a coined class while, positing an object the sentence never introduces and losing the duration meaning entirely.
Making that while-entity the Theme unpacks the non-literal "take a while" into a literal taking event, which the idiom coherence test rules out (nothing is grasped or transferred).

q2_gaps: vague duration NPs with no number or unit ("a while", "a long time") — duration is only (Measure e duration <n> <unit>), with a fallback only for bare-plural durations ("for days" -> MeasureAtLeast ... 2 <unit>)
the light-verb duration predication "X takes a while" (the subject lasts/requires an indefinitely long time)
a bare demonstrative "that" with no antecedent — the no-antecedent pronoun rule enumerates he/she/they/it only, and the event-anaphora rule for "that" presupposes an antecedent clause
notes: (Might sk_take_1) at (STV 1.0 0.9) with no tense atom beside it is exactly the instructed handling of epistemic "could", and Agent on the inanimate, stative transitive subject follows the instruction as written.
